digest.component_or_area: src/rebar codebase-wide comment and docstring rationalization
propositions: ~2,033 lines of recoverable comments (history, rationale, contracts) across 439 files in src/rebar are mislocated per taxonomy: history belongs in tickets, architecture in ADRs, logic in code, contracts in schema.

Six subsystem shards identified and applied five dispositions (RELOCATE/DELETE/KEEP/DO_NOT_MOVE/CORRECT-IN-PLACE) to every comment block, with load-bearing invariants (replay-compat, security seals, API workarounds, lint pragmas) preserved verbatim and recorded in do_not_move lists.

Three files (event_append.py, _processors.py, signing.py) retain nearly all their comments because their inline blocks encode live security and replay-compatibility invariants that cannot be relocated; their real architectural split is out of scope.

Verified-stale comments (e.g., DET_CHECKS docs claiming P1-P9 while code runs P1-P11, Anthropic constraints already retracted as 'relics', obsolete import sequencing notes) are corrected in place where they document active invariants, not deleted.
Eight sites carry the same four-paragraph argument ('one idempotent transform, fit-then-normalize, local-side only') restated independently; consolidated into a single ADR 0062 with inline citations.

Net recovery across six shards is ~85 lines (measured, not estimated) delivered primarily through relocation to ADRs 0062-0069 and collapsing inline blocks to one-line citations, with three shards (ad16, ab77, 9ce8) adding net lines because corrections and moves dominate deletions.
